newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Astra to seek national car privileges.
newsitem.headline: Astra to seek national car privileges.

text.p: Indonesia's largest automobile manufacturer PT Astra International will seek national car status for two models it produces within the next two years, company president director Muhammad 'Bob' Hasan said.

He told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that a sedan produced by Astra in collaboration with Daihatsu of Japan will contain over 60 percent local components by the beginning of 1998, making it eligible for tax and tariff benefits under the national car programme.
He said the Kijang, Astra's most popular brand and manufactured in collaboration with Toyota Motor Company, will reach 60 percent local content by 1999 and be eligible for similar benefits.
Indonesia's national car programme or Mobnas grants wide tax and tariff breaks for automobiles which meet local content requirements.
The only company so far eligible for the benefits is PT Timor Putra Nasional, controlled by the youngest son of President Suharto.

The decision to allow only one company the privileges under the Mobnas programme has seen Japan, the United States and the European Union accuse Indonesia of violating World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules.
Jakarta is now negotiating with all three under the WTO's arbitration guidelines.
The subsidies allow the 1600 c.c. sedan manufactured in collaboration with Kia Motors of South Korea, to be sold at about half the sticker price of comparable models.
Timor Putra has promised to meet local content requirments within three years.
"The Mobnas is not only for Timor, but it is also for any other brand whenever they will be able to cover 60 percent of their production locally," Hasan said.
"They will automatically be given Mobnas-type of incentives," he said.
Local content in both the Kijang and the Daihatsu sedan were currently at about 45 percent, he said.
Hasan was speaking on the eve of the inauguration of a pulp mill in East Kalimantan province on Wednesday by President Suharto.
Hasan, who is a close associate of the president and his regular golf partner, owns almost all the equity of the mill through the Kalismanis timber conglomerate.
Astra would also manufacture a completely indigenously produced motorcycle by the end of this year, he said.
A strong growth in Astra's motorcycle sales boosted the company's net profit figures in the first quarter of this year to 119.83 billion rupiah from 73.46 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
The firm expects sales of Honda motorcycles to reach one million by the end of 1997 compared to the 654,262 units it sold in 1996.

The company is scheduled to announce half-year results next week and corporate finance director Rini Suwandi said they would be positive despite last month's weakening of the rupiah currency which she said had raised costs.
She refused to give details.
Suwandi has said previously she expected the company to post a net profit of 627 billion rupiah in 1997, up from 470 billion posted in 1996.
